why.text: Bierzo is an Atlantic-continental basin with mild temperatures and plenty of sun. Fair rainfall and acid soils give fresh, fruity wines.

styles.text: Fresh whites, rosados and claretes; fresh, structured reds with red or black fruit, and oak when aged.

climate.text: Atlantic-continental transition in a tectonic basin: mild temperatures, fairly abundant rain, many hours of sun.

tastes.text: Whites: steely to golden yellow; fruity or floral, fresh. Rosés: light pink to ruby red; red or black fruit, fresh. Reds: violet to red; red or black fruit, violets; fresh, structured. Aged reds add vanilla, toast or spice.

why.text: Winters are long and harsh, with strong summer sun and about 500 mm of rain. Hot summer days give Prieto Picudo its intense aroma.

styles.text: Whites of Albarín Blanco, Verdejo and Godello; Prieto Picudo rosados; fleshy, aromatic reds, also aged. Semi-sweet and sweet wines are also made.

climate.text: Continental: long, harsh winter, irregular summer alternating very hot dry spells with cold ones, about 500 mm rain, much sun.

tastes.text: Whites: balanced, fresh, complex. Rosés (Prieto Picudo): very aromatic, fresh. Reds: strong colour; red and black fruit; fleshy, full, lightly astringent, persistent. Aged reds: more complex; the astringency disappears in oak.

styles.name: Tinto envejecido
styles.text: Prieto Picudo with more complexity, no astringency left, tannic, great mouthfeel.

why.text: Altitude and an extreme continental climate slow ripening. Tinta del País wines come out rich in polyphenols and acidity.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; the reds stand up well to long ageing in oak barrels. Sweet reds and ice wine (Vino de Hielo) are also made.

climate.text: Extreme continental, with a strong temperature contrast between day and night; altitude is a key factor.

soil.text: Sandy loam, low in organic matter. Soils in the middle of the area are basic and rich in calcium. The Campiña plains have more clay in the north and more carbonates in the south-west. The Páramos del Cerrato have active limestone and marly clays.

tastes.text: Whites: steely to golden yellow; fruity, balanced, fresh. Rosés: onion skin to strawberry red; red or black fruit. Reds: violet-red to purple; red or black fruit; balanced, fresh. Aged wines: wood and fruit aromas; reds are dry.

styles.name: Tinto envejecido
styles.text: Garnet to brick red; wood-and-fruit aromas; bears long oak ageing well.

styles.name: Rosado envejecido
styles.text: Onion skin to raspberry pink with ageing tones; red fruit and wood aromas.

why.text: An extreme, arid continental climate and poor, well-drained soils let Prieto Picudo ripen. The wines are red-fruited with a slight spritz.

styles.text: Fruity whites with aniseed notes; very fruity rosados; red-fruited reds, also aged.

climate.text: Extreme, arid continental climate with low rainfall (350 to 550 mm a year).

soil.text: Mostly brown limy soils of sandy loam, 50 to 60 cm deep. They are low in fertility but well drained and aerated.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow; very fruity with aniseed notes; medium-high body. Rosés: picota and cherry; red fruit, lively, slight sparkle. Reds: bluish tones; red ripe fruit; high structure. Aged: wood, fruit remains.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva
styles.text: Aged red; more complex, wood appears, fruit stays.

why.text: Vines line the Pisuerga, and 30 % are over 60 years old. Grapes ripen with balanced acidity and sugar, giving wines with a local stamp.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, young or aged; also sweet wines and quality sparkling, white or rosé.

climate.text: Valley midway down the Pisuerga, between the cold climate upstream and the milder one at its mouth.

soil.text: Tertiary and Quaternary sediments rest on clays and marls. The soil is sandy with plenty of gravel, and poor in organic matter. Lime ranges from 1% to 35%. The pH is about 8.1.

tastes.text: Whites: clear yellow; fruity, fresh, light. Rosés: strawberry to cherry; fresh or ripe fruit. Reds: picota to vermilion; wild berries, wood when aged; medium body. Sweet wines: same profile, with more aroma and volume.

styles.name: Vino dulce
styles.text: White, rosé or red; aromas and volume boosted by sugar.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: White or rosé sparkling; fruity, clean, broad flavours.

why.text: Tempranillo grows in a high, strongly continental climate with big temperature swings. It gains balanced acidity and sweet tannins, suited to ageing.

styles.text: Very aromatic Albillo Mayor whites; rosados with lively colour and fruit; young reds fruity and intense, aged reds complex and elegant.

climate.text: Strongly continental: big yearly and daily temperature swings, especially at ripening, moderate to low rainfall and high average altitude.

soil.text: Ochre and reddish sandy clays lie beside the Duero’s middle and low terraces. The pH is basic. Organic matter is scarce.

tastes.text: Whites: very aromatic, fruity or herbal; fresh acidity. Rosés: vivid colours, fruity nose; refreshing, light. Reds: vivid colour, deep; fruity and intense when young. Aged reds: lasting blue tones; complex fruit and wood; powerful yet elegant.

styles.name: Tinto envejecido
styles.text: Vivid colour, lasting blue tones; complex fruit and wood; powerful yet elegant.

why.text: The vineyards are high and dry, on clay with pebbles. Tempranillo here gives fresh, mineral wines rich in phenols.

styles.text: Rosados and young or aged reds; the reds show some mineral tones.

climate.text: Mediterranean with continental influence, average altitude above 800 m: long harsh winters, mild summers, little rain, large daily swings.

soil.text: Medium texture, high in clay, with gravel and rounded stones.

tastes.text: Rosés: cherry pink; fruity with floral touches; medium structure. Young reds: intense red; frank, intense aromas; tasty, good structure. Aged reds: intense red with ageing tones; tasty, balanced. Mineral tones stand out most in the reds.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva
styles.text: Intense red with ageing tones; frank, intense aromas; tasty, good structure.

why.text: Old vines face harsh winters and long hours of sun on iron-rich sandy-loam soils. The wines are very deeply coloured and high in alcohol.

styles.text: Whites (some barrel-fermented) and rosados; structured, tannic reds with ripe fruit and lower acidity than elsewhere. Quality sparkling wines and semi-dry to sweet wines are also made.

climate.text: Extremely cold winters, many hours of sun and extreme temperatures.

soil.text: Sandy loam with little organic matter. The pH is slightly acid to neutral (6-7), about 8 in the south-west. Poor in trace elements except iron.

tastes.text: Whites: pale to golden yellow; fruity, floral or herbal. Rosés: pale pink to salmon; fresh red or black fruit. Reds: picota to ruby red; red or black fruit; structured, tannic, lower acidity; barrel tones when aged.

styles.name: Fermentado en barrica
styles.text: White fermented in barrel; fruit mixed with smoky, toasty wood tones.

why.text: Old vines on alluvial soils get little rain and much sun. The grapes ripen evenly and gain sugar, giving deeply coloured, structured reds.

styles.text: Aromatic whites (some barrel-fermented), claretes and rosados; tannic, long-lived reds, also aged.

climate.text: Mediterranean, strongly continental: 350 to 400 mm rain, dry summers, harsh winters, large day-night swings, spring frost.

soil.text: Deep alluvial soils, poor in organic matter.

tastes.text: Whites: ripe-fruit primary aromas; barrel-fermented ones add smoke and toast. Claretes and rosés: very aromatic, tasty, balanced. Reds: intense colour, high tannin, much structure, long-lived.

styles.name: Clarete
styles.text: Very aromatic, tasty and balanced.

styles.name: Crianza, Reserva, Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red of great colour intensity, tannic and structured; very long-lived.

why.text: A high plateau at 700 to 870 m has big day-night swings. Grapes gain sugar while keeping their acidity.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, reds, quality sparkling and fortified (vino de licor) wines.

climate.text: Continental by altitude: long cold winters, late spring frost, hot dry summers, 400 to 430 mm rain, mean 11.5 °C.

soil.text: Brown soils on stony deposits: quartzite pebbles, reddish clays and sands; marls and limestone in places.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to amber, gold or green tones; fruit, floral, herbal; fresh, medium to full body. Rosés: strawberry to onion-skin; red fruit. Reds: ruby to picota; black and red fruit; oak-aged ones add yeast or bakery notes and oak.

styles.name: Dorado
styles.text: Golden fortified wine; yeast, toast, smoke, spice and dried nuts.

styles.name: Pálido
styles.text: Straw to pale gold fortified wine from biological ageing; almonds, yeast.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: White or rosé sparkling; fine bubble, floral and fruity, bakery notes.

why.text: Canyon vineyards on granite and slate are warmer and wetter than the rest of the region. Juan García gives wines with structure and softness.

styles.text: Whites, rosados, orange wines and reds, young or aged; reds are rich in polyphenols with ripe fruit aromas.

climate.text: Sub-humid Mediterranean, warmer and wetter than the region: 575 to 800 mm rain; canyon valleys about 5 °C warmer than the plateau.

soil.text: Acid granite and slate soils: silty sand, stony, shallow (about 30 cm), poor in lime and organic matter.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow with grey to gold tints; fruity or floral, sometimes mineral. Rosés: pale pink to light red; fruity. Reds: violet to purple red; fruity or mineral; aged reds show wood.

styles.name: Vino naranja
styles.text: Amber orange wine; fruity or floral, stone fruit and citrus, fuller body.

styles.name: Fermentado en Barrica
styles.text: Fermented and lees-aged in oak barrels; smoky, toasty notes mixed with fruit.

why.text: Terraced slopes on acid slate soils have a mild, damp Mediterranean microclimate. Rufete gives mineral wines of medium-high alcohol and long life.

styles.text: Whites and rosados of medium structure; young reds and reds aged in barrel. All are long-lived.

climate.text: Particular microclimate: mild, humid Mediterranean, with vineyards on terraced slopes.

soil.text: Acid soils, mostly sandy loam. Slate lies to the west and granite to the east.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow; fruity, floral or herbal; medium structure. Rosés: onion-skin to cherry pink; fruity, floral or herbal. Reds: red; fruity, floral or herbal; medium-high acidity, medium-low structure. All show mineral and scrub-herb notes.

styles.name: Tinto envejecido en barrica
styles.text: Red aged in barrel; long-lived, very suited to keeping.

why.text: Mostly old Garnacha vines grow on south-facing granite slopes, some above 1,000 m. They give fresh wines despite hot, dry summers.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, young and barrel-aged; reds age well.

climate.text: Mediterranean with a continental touch: hot, dry summers, short mild winters, 400 to 800 mm of rain, mean 12 to 15 °C.

soil.text: Sandy loam over granite, slightly acid and poor in organic matter; some schist.

altitude.text: Some plots above 1,000 m; vines mostly on south-facing slopes.

tastes.text: Whites: straw to golden yellow; fruity, tasty, balanced. Rosés: pale pink to raspberry; red and black fruit. Reds: picota red, violet rims; red and black fruit, dry. Barrel-aged: wood, toast, spice.

styles.name: Envejecido en barrica
styles.text: Barrel-aged; riper fruit with wood, toast and spice; softer, more persistent.

why.text: An extreme climate with a wide day-night temperature swing ripens the grapes slowly, giving deeply coloured, structured wines.

styles.text: Reds: single-grape (at least 12 months in oak) or blended (at least 6). Whites: single-grape or blended, steel tank or at least 3 months in oak.

climate.text: Markedly continental, with Atlantic cloud. Rain is moderate, about 490 mm a year, and summers are dry. Recorded extremes: 42 °C and -20 °C.

soil.text: Sandy to clay-loam, weakly alkaline and low in organic matter. A sand cover, centimetres to metres thick, hides varied soils.

altitude.text: Vines on the river terrace; river at 725 m, plateaus at 880 m.

tastes.text: Whites: straw yellow to golden; stone fruit or citrus; balanced acidity. Reds: violet-red to tile red; red and black fruit; medium to high structure and length. Oak-aged reds add balsamic or spice notes.

styles.name: Vino Tinto Monovarietal
styles.text: Red from one authorised red grape; at least 12 months in oak.

styles.name: Vino Tinto Multivarietal
styles.text: Blended red; at least 6 months in oak.

styles.name: Vino Blanco Multivarietal
styles.text: Blended white; steel tank or at least 3 months in oak.

why.text: Warm, poor soil of sand and gravel in a sheltered valley floor helps the grapes ripen and gain colour and tannin.

styles.text: Young and oak-aged reds and rosados. Ageing is in oak barrels of 225 to 600 l or wooden vats up to 5,500 l.

climate.text: A milder microclimate, with a mean of 12 °C a year and good west-east airflow. It has 206 frost-free days; neighbouring areas have under 200.

soil.text: Sandy river-terrace soil (about 78% sand) with stones and gravel; warm, free-draining and poor in organic matter.

altitude.text: Valley floor at about 720 m, between plateaus of 800 to 840 m.

tastes.text: Reds: deep, steady colour with blue-red tones; ripe red and black fruit; sweet, long-lived tannin; medium-to-full body; long finish. Rosés: onion skin to redcurrant; red or black fruit; fresh, balanced.

styles.name: Vino Tinto Joven
styles.text: Young red: cold soak, steel tank, at least 21 days of maceration.

styles.name: Vino Tinto Monovarietal
styles.text: Single-grape red aged in 225 to 600 l oak barrels or wooden vats.

styles.name: Vino Tinto Multivarietal
styles.text: Blended red aged in 225 to 600 l oak barrels or wooden vats.

why.text: Poor, well-drained soils give wines rich in extract and in colour pigments (anthocyanins).

styles.text: Rosados and reds, young or oak-aged. Ageing is in French and American oak barrels.

climate.text: Semi-arid Mediterranean, with about 410 mm of rain a year. The mean is 11.4 °C, with 2,650 sun hours. June to September are dry.

soil.text: Sandy clay loam with stones; medium-low fertility and organic matter; drains well. Alfisols and inceptisols.

tastes.text: Rosés: onion-skin to raspberry pink; fresh fruit with floral or caramel notes; fresh. Reds: purple to tile red; red and black fruit, with spice when oak-aged; medium to full body and length.

styles.name: Vino rosado
styles.text: Onion-skin to raspberry-pink rosé; cold skin maceration, then temperature-controlled fermentation.

styles.name: Vino tinto
styles.text: Red with a cold soak below 10 °C for at least 24 hours.
